before: This article addresses adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy cyber-physical systems (CPSs) affected by stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. Since nonlinear CPSs face cyber-layer attacks as well as physical-layer component failures, while their communication resources are often limited, an adaptive event-triggered mechanism (AETM) is employed to reduce redundant network transmissions through dynamic adjustment of the triggering threshold based on real-time state-error information. Specifically, stochastic deception attacks are characterized by a Bernoulli process, and actuator failures are modeled by Markov switching fault matrices. Accordingly, a unified closed-loop model is established. Then, a looped functional dependent on fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) is constructed to exploit membership-function information and sampled-data dynamics. Based on this functional, stability criteria are obtained to guarantee asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system while achieving a prescribed H∞ disturbance attenuation level. Moreover, joint design of the controller gains and adaptive triggering parameters is formulated through tractable linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Validation is finally carried out with an engineering-motivated permanent magnet synchronous motor example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy system to demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the developed method.
after: This article addresses adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy cyber-physical systems (CPSs) subject to stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. An adaptive event-triggered mechanism (AETM) adjusts the transmission threshold using state-error information to reduce redundant communication. Deception attacks are described by a Bernoulli process, and actuator failures are represented by Markov switching fault matrices. These components are incorporated into a unified closed-loop model. The signs of the membership-function derivatives define operational regions for a region-dependent fuzzy controller. Within this framework, the controller gains and event-triggering weight matrices are jointly designed. A two-sided looped functional dependent on fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) incorporates membership information and sampled-data dynamics. Sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability with a prescribed H∞ disturbance attenuation level are formulated as linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). A permanent magnet synchronous motor example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy example illustrate the control responses and the reduction in data transmissions.

before: This study has addressed adaptive event-triggered H∞ control of IT-2 fuzzy CPSs affected simultaneously by stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. An AETM has been employed to limit unnecessary data transmissions by updating the triggering threshold online using real-time state-error information. In addition, a region-dependent piecewise fuzzy control strategy has been developed by incorporating derivative information from the membership functions. Based on an FMF-dependent and time-dependent looped functional, stability criteria have been obtained to guarantee closed-loop asymptotic stability while achieving a prescribed H∞ disturbance attenuation level. The controller gains and adaptive event-triggering weight matrices have been jointly determined through tractable LMIs, while a bounding technique has been employed to address the norm-bounded uncertainty induced by Markov-type actuator failures.
after: This study has considered adaptive event-triggered H∞ control of IT-2 fuzzy CPSs subject to stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. The AETM updates its threshold using state-error information to reduce redundant transmissions. Membership-function derivative information defines operational regions for the fuzzy control design. An FMF-dependent looped functional is used to formulate sufficient stability and performance conditions. The controller gains and event-triggering weight matrices are jointly determined through LMIs, with a bounding technique used to handle actuator-failure uncertainty.
